source.digest_scope: git diff --binary and SHA256 lines for every untracked file except this evidence file

environment.browser: Codex in-app browser against an isolated portal with a fake root control service
environment.target: Ubuntu 24.04 LLMCtl with systemd, Docker, OmniRoute, and NVIDIA GPU Workers

evidence: 17 OmniRoute lifecycle tests passed using real temporary SQLite databases and a deterministic Docker/systemd runner.
Assessment covered deep integrity, foreign-key violations, WAL, free pages, disk headroom, and stale backup recommendations.
Online backup used sqlite3 backup, quick_check, SHA256, size, ownership, and mode metadata; manual rollback restored the exact business row and image configuration.
Online maintenance created a backup and preserved data without issuing any Router or systemd command.
Maintenance-window compaction executed stop, VACUUM, restart, and full smoke semantics; injected smoke failure restored the pre-maintenance snapshot.
A failed Router stop restarted the account portal without touching the database.
A corrupted current database was preserved as a non-restorable incident DB/WAL/SHM copy before a verified snapshot was restored.
A tampered backup was rejected by size/SHA256 validation before any systemd command.
Mutable image tags, wrong confirmations, path traversal, non-OmniRoute mode, active model jobs, and interrupted controller tasks all failed closed.
A successful fixed-image upgrade pulled the image, recorded its immutable image ID, backed up SQLite, switched both compatible image keys, restarted Router, and ran full smoke semantics.
Injected post-start smoke failure restored the original database, image configuration, and running image.
A configured/running image drift was rejected before backup creation because the original runtime could not be reproduced reliably.
A running image ID different from the ID inspected after pull triggered automatic database and image rollback.
The published 3.8.49 Docker manifest was inspected as available for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. No production image was pulled or started.
The llmctl entry point loaded cmd_omniroute, omniroute_wait_job, and omniroute_request successfully with LLMCTL_SOURCE_ONLY=1.
bash -n passed for llmctl.sh, every lib/llmctl module, and install-llm-cluster.sh.
The legacy llmctl update --omniroute-image path delegates to the backup-protected state machine and rejects a combined vLLM/OmniRoute update.
2 portal permission/forwarding tests proved administrator-only access and exact mapping to status, assess, submit, job, and cancel allowlist operations.
High-frequency job polling produced no audit event, while assessment, submission, and cancellation remained audited.
20 model deployment tests passed, including construction with the shared OmniRoute submission lock; model and Router mutations cannot be submitted concurrently.
36 static/source/upgrade-package tests passed, and the new Python and Shell modules are present in the installer and upgrade manifest.
50 frontend tests passed across 9 files.
The OmniRoute composable tests covered status/recommended image loading, deep assessment, and exact update/rollback payloads.
The portal production build passed with 30 transformed modules.
Built portal index SHA256: e9a1b4c228a9e23c695d032d539d1ea28af8206f16ebf698b25f8f23aaea61b0.
Built portal CSS SHA256: b05bb3440bf398a344dceb8a44bcd09da8fc06ff16d4a069eac8c96bc1282a50.
Built portal JavaScript SHA256: e1e4a4772d6f52787573d8e1ed196efe74ce1e795aa96a5220b0f68025104ae1.
265 Python tests passed in 56.560 seconds.
Python compilation, strict JSON parsing, bash syntax, command-module loading, and git diff whitespace checks passed.
All modified handwritten sources remained below 3000 physical lines; App.vue had 2979 lines, llmctl.sh 2870, model_deployment.py 2524, and omniroute_maintenance.py 1350.
The administrator navigation exposed OmniRoute 维护 and rendered configured/running/recommended images, database/WAL/SHM sizes, assessment status, recommendations, actions, tasks, and backup inventory.
Online maintenance, compaction, and update buttons were disabled by default and for a wrong phrase, then enabled only for MAINTAIN ONLINE, COMPACT SQLITE, and UPDATE OMNIROUTE respectively.
Rollback remained disabled until the exact selected backup ID was included in the ROLLBACK phrase.
Read-only assessment produced visible warning feedback; an isolated backup task reached 100 percent, showed a success result, and added a second backup row.
At a 680-pixel viewport the summary and action sections used one column, the backup table scrolled inside its container, and body scrollWidth equaled clientWidth.

A final run against the final built assets showed one maintenance heading, one healthy assessment, the backup ID and SHA256 prefix, an initially disabled upgrade action, and no page-level horizontal overflow.

gates.reason: shellcheck is not installed in the local development environment. Bash parsing, module loading, static contracts, and command-source tests passed, but shellcheck diagnostics were not executed.
No real Ubuntu systemd service, Docker Router, production storage.sqlite, or GPU-backed full smoke was modified or executed from this development machine.
required_actions: Run sudo llmctl upgrade, then sudo llmctl model init if the model-control socket is not ready.
Run sudo llmctl omniroute status and sudo llmctl omniroute sqlite assess --deep; confirm no critical result and sufficient disk headroom.
Create a managed backup and verify it appears under /var/backups/llmctl/omniroute and in the WebUI backup inventory.

During a maintenance window, upgrade with sudo llmctl omniroute update diegosouzapw/omniroute:3.8.49 and confirm the task reaches succeeded, the actual image ID changes, /v1 passes full smoke, and GPU Workers remain running.
Keep the printed backup ID until production traffic, dashboard, API keys, Combos, call logs, and portal reconciliation have been accepted.

final_stage: Implemented and locally verified; not deployed or production-accepted
